messages:
anya: Quick thread to capture follow-ups from today's design jam: proposal to split thin router into a low-latency routing shim (ripcord) and move enrichment out-of-path. This is a long refactor; I'm proposing concrete checkpoints we can measure.

sam: Love it. Can you list checkpoints? that helps scope.

anya: Checkpoint A: ripcord read-only proxy deployed behind feature flag, zero writes, traffic mirrored for telemetry only. Checkpoint B: controlled canary where ripcord handles read routing for 5% of requests from opt-in tenants. Checkpoint C: dual-write path for session metadata with transactional guard and backpressure. Checkpoint D: full cutover for non-SLA tenants, with auto-fallback policy. Checkpoint E: decommission old router once steady-state metrics meet targets for 2 weeks.

matt: For each checkpoint we need explicit SLO gates and an owner. Suggest: A (sam), B (matt), C (meera), D (jen), E (mikel/sre).

meera: Migration concerns: session races, key-prefix collisions in KV, enrichment ordering. For dual-write (C) we must provide a conflict detector and a reconciliation job that surfaces anomalies. Can't accept silent divergence.

sam: Implementation note: ripcord will be a very small binary that only understands routing headers and tenant affinity. No enrichment hooks in A/B. For sticky sessions we'll include a header X-Ripcord-Session that both systems understand. If absent, fall back to proxy.

jen: Can we have a rollback circuit that flips per-tenant? Need that to minimize blast radius.

anya: Yes; feature flags will be per-tenant and per-pop. Example flag payload we'll use in rollout service:

```json
{"flags": {"ripcord.enabled": false, "ripcord.canary_tenants": ["test-co"], "ripcord.pop_allowlist": ["us-west-2"]}}
```

matt: Metric set to monitor during canary: request success rate, p95 latency, redis/KV miss ratio, enrichment lag (ms), and cost-per-token approximation. Add a synthetic load that's representative.

meera: I'll add a small regression test that replays production traces against ripcord in replay mode to detect ordering or state issues before phase C.

sam: Ops: need a runbook stub for automatic rollback thresholds. Proposed auto-rollback if p99 latency increases >20% from baseline or error rate increases >0.2% sustained over 5m. Also a manual abort flow if reconciliation job finds >0.1% divergent keys in 1h window.

jen: Do we have capacity/cost impact estimates? ripcord might affect batching behavior.

matt: Good call. We'll run a cost delta experiment during B: measure CPU/GPU token throughput and per-request cpu-millis. If cost delta > 1.15x for a tenant cohort, rollback that cohort.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pipeline created: ripcord/canary/1766012345. Logs: https://ci.internal/ripcord/canary/1766012345

anya: I'll open the RFC follow-up doc with phases, the exact flags and the gating rules, plus owners and runbook links. Action items: Sam: small shim PR (A), Meera: replay harness and migration checker, Matt: canary dashboard and synthetic profile, Jen: runbook draft + rollback automation.

meera: I'll also add instrumentation tags: trace span attribute "component=ripcord" and "phase=<A|B|C|D>" so Optimize can later attribute regressions.

sam: One more thought: KV topology. Option 1: per-pop shard ownership; Option 2: central cached store with a routing layer. I prefer per-pop shards to keep hotpath low-latency, but we need a plan to migrate prefixes.

matt: Per-pop shard seems ideal for latency. Migration pattern: prefix writes to new shard during C, leave reads reading old shard until reconciliation completes. Then swap reads to new shard in a controlled window.

jen: Sounds good. Keep the initial surface small. No enrichment extraction in A/B. We'll only do routing + session affinity.

anya: Agreed. I'll post the RFC follow-up with checklist and include estimated sprint counts for each checkpoint. We'll discuss owners in the next arch sync. Thanks all.
